source.original_title: 06/03/2026 - Tim Wigg x Ben Byrne KL
source.display_title: 06/03/2026 - Tim Wigg x Ben Byrne KL — Follow Up

prospect.name: Tim Wigg
prospect.occupation: Owner of an electrical contracting business; also runs a record label and promotes music events
prospect.family_status: Married; wife is French (referred to as Nat), a florist; no children mentioned
prospect.training_background: Degree in exercise science / human movement; strength and conditioning coaching for Surfing Australia in his 20s. Twelve months with an online PT coach (UK coach based in Bali) on an upper/lower/full-body split plus an 1800-calorie diet; dropped from 84 kg to 72 kg, now back to 78 kg. Ended that coaching ~6 weeks ago. Currently back in the gym ~3 days/week, surfs, does mobility work and rowing.
prospect.medical: Contracted shingles immediately after a high-stress commercial project and worked through it; reports the episode ended roughly three to four weeks before the call. Reports recurring aches and postural imbalance he attributes to years wearing a tool belt: 'my body sort of starts to tell me... starts to create some pains'. The rep asked no health, injury or medication questions at any point.

signals: Lost ground during a hard season: 14-hour days, one day off in six weeks, then shingles; regained 6 kg of the 12 kg he had lost
Explicit regret framing about how he ran his business and himself: 'I've sort of seen where I've gone wrong in the past and why things haven't worked'
Overlaps with the_optimizer — self-rates physique 5-6/10 and wants 10, is a business owner and health-literate — but price was a genuine barrier, which does not fit the optimizer definition

goals.text: Find a lifelong, sustainable programme rather than another short cycle — 'something that's going to be part of my lifestyle moving forwards'
Drop back down from 78 kg toward the 72 kg he previously reached
Build strength and even out the body after years in a tool belt — 'develop that sort of evenness through my body'
Improve mobility and posture; already stretches and hangs daily
Train explosively in a way that carries over to surfing
Minimalist home setup in the backyard so training does not depend on a gym or travel
Have the routine and holistic habits locked in before he and his wife move to France in a couple of years
Learn to use kettlebells properly as a skill — 'it's like an apprenticeship in how to use a kettlebell'

pains.text: Fourteen-hour days and one day off in six weeks on a commercial project collapsed his training and he regained weight
Previous coach dismissed his workload as 'noise' and he felt judged rather than supported — 'getting a whack across the knuckles every Wednesday'
Cannot sustain training when work spikes; historically falls off and has to restart
Aches and postural imbalance from wearing a tool belt for years, which worsen when he stops training
Got shingles off the back of the project and had to keep working through it
Time-poor for researching and building his own programme despite an exercise science background
Dislikes gyms and does not want to depend on one — 'I'm not a big fan of gyms'
Undercharging and saying yes to unprofitable commercial jobs, which he links to putting himself last

objections.raw_quote: Okay. Yeah, that's a bit more than what I was expecting. So, yeah. Yeah, I wasn't sure what we were looking at here with the pricing.
objections.rep_response: Asked for the exchange rate, then without isolating the objection or taking any financial picture, volunteered a cheaper option: an improvised three-month tier at $4,000

objections.raw_quote: I'm paying my business coach $1,600 a month, so $1,400 on top of that's going to be a bit of a stretch
objections.rep_response: Asked 'is it the total that's the issue or is it like the monthly', got 'the monthly', then offered the $4,000 three-month tier at three payments of $1,500 — a higher monthly than the objection he had just isolated

objections.raw_quote: can I, can I like just have a bit of pondering time, like 48 hours or something like that, just work out
objections.rep_response: Accepted it without running any part of the think-about-it play; moved to arranging WhatsApp follow-up

objections.raw_quote: I just need to kind of probably discuss it with my wife as well because she's been like, I want me to try and reduce my coaching
objections.rep_response: Asked one clarifying question, 'She wants you to reduce your coaching?', then let it drop and did not run the spouse play

offer.payment_plan_terms: Improvised live. For the 6-month tier: 'split it up half and half', or three payments of $2,000, or six payments of $1,200 described as the $6,000 'with a bit of interest at it' — an unstated total of $7,200. For the improvised 3-month $4,000 tier: three payments of $1,500 — an unstated total of $4,500.

evidence: Prospect asked for time: 'can I like just have a bit of pondering time, like 48 hours or something like that'
No payment taken and no payment link mentioned at any point

Counter-evidence of buying intent: 'I would say I prefer to lock in for the six month option, but I just need to kind of look at a couple of things financially from my end' and 'I'm really pumped, to be honest, to get into something'
Follow-up channel agreed and WhatsApp contact exchanged on the call; no second call booked
outcome.next_step: Prospect to review his budget and possible subscription cuts and message the rep on WhatsApp within a couple of days; no date set and no call booked

notable.note: The rep invented a three-month $4,000 tier live on the call in response to price hesitation, and quoted two instalment plans whose totals ($7,200 and $4,500) exceed the headline prices he attached them to without ever stating those totals. He also ran no health or injury screening whatsoever despite the prospect disclosing recent shingles and recurring pain, and he skipped the consequence frame and commitment check entirely before revealing price.

quality.notes: Repeated label inversions on short turns and on some long ones. Examples: at 00:06:05 the rep's label carries the prospect's line 'So I sort of just struggled'; at 00:06:08 the prospect's label carries the rep's question 'What changed?'; at 00:56:26 the prospect's label carries the rep's pricing line 'the longer people sign up for, we give them a bit of a discount'; the 00:51:16-00:52:00 exchange about the business coach is inverted throughout. Role was read from content in every case.
